claims.exact_claim: With cancel-in-progress: false, a new run does not cancel the running workflow through this concurrency setting, but it can replace a pending run.
claims.original_anchor: With `cancel-in-progress: false`, the running workflow can finish, but a waiting run can still be replaced.
claims.qualification: The group and repository scope is given later in the original; this is not a guarantee against unrelated cancellation.

claims.exact_claim: queue: single is the default and permits one pending run per concurrency group; a new arrival cancels and replaces that pending run.
claims.original_anchor: In the default `queue: single` mode, a concurrency group has room for one pending run. A new arrival cancels that pending run and takes its place.

claims.exact_claim: The described contention operates among runs sharing a concurrency group in the same repository.
claims.original_anchor: This applies when the runs use the same group in the same repository.

claims.exact_claim: queue: max retains up to 100 pending runs in a group and cancels additional arrivals once the queue is full.
claims.original_anchor: Set `queue: max` to retain multiple waiting runs. GitHub allows up to 100 pending runs in that group and cancels further arrivals when the queue is full.

claims.exact_claim: Queued runs are processed in the order they start waiting on the concurrency group; workflow dispatch order is not guaranteed.
claims.original_anchor: They are processed in the order they begin waiting on the concurrency group, which can differ from workflow dispatch order.
claims.qualification: They means retained waiting runs, not the rejected arrivals immediately before this sentence.

claims.exact_claim: Keeping cancel-in-progress: false is compatible with queue: max; combining queue: max and cancel-in-progress: true causes workflow validation to fail.
claims.original_anchor: Keep `cancel-in-progress: false` with that configuration. Combining `queue: max` with `cancel-in-progress: true` fails workflow validation.
claims.qualification: Explicit false is a valid configuration choice, not a claim that the property must be written when omitted.

claims.exact_claim: With the default queue, cancel-in-progress: true also cancels the currently running workflow in the concurrency group.
claims.original_anchor: With the default queue, setting `cancel-in-progress: true` also cancels the currently running workflow in the group.

claims.exact_claim: Disabling cancellation of in-progress runs alone does not guarantee execution of every waiting run.
claims.original_anchor: Disabling it therefore protects active work without guaranteeing that every waiting run will execute.
claims.qualification: Inference from pending replacement and the bounded queue; protects refers only to cancellation by this setting.

scope_cuts: Case-insensitive group naming and dynamic group expressions are documented background but are not needed to answer this question.
source_notes: Current normative property documentation includes queue: max. Do not replace this with an older blanket claim that only one pending run is ever supported.
Use the normative queue and cancel-in-progress property definitions; some generic explanatory examples describe cancellation without repeating the cancel-in-progress condition.
